uncited: *   **Input:** A 3D dataset, a set of Regions of Interest (defined as 3D bounding boxes), transfer functions, and a hierarchy of Layers and Drawables.
**View:** The central display component associated with a compositing camera and viewport.
A Layer may be composited multiple times with different materials.
**Material:** Contains attributes (color, opacity) and a GLSL shader program.
The shader implements the rendering functionality for the Material.
A Null Layer is a layer containing zero drawables.
It is generated using shaders that have access to system texture resources.
**Per-Layer Rendering:** Traditional volume rendering is applied to the small ROIs defined within each Layer.
**Compositing Phase:** The resulting layer textures are composited together.
When an entity changes (e.g., a material property), an event fires to all shared Drawables.
These Drawables fire events to their parent Layers.
The following pseudocode illustrates the event-driven dataflow and hierarchy management.
The compositing phase is generally $O(N)$ with respect to the number of layers, assuming standard 2D compositing operations.
